featured_reviews.name: Avijit Chakrovorty
featured_reviews.review_text:
I stayed in Flat 303, Building 4, Man Opus, owned by Ms. Jyoti Kumari and Mr Divesh, and I want to share my experience to help future tenants make informed decisions.

When I moved in, the flat was heavily infested with cockroaches - an issue I discovered only after moving in. Despite informing the landlord immediately, I had to arrange professional pest control every few months, but the infestation never fully improved.

I had paid 50% painting charges before moving in, and my agreement clearly stated that I wouldn’t owe painting costs at move-out. I followed every clause of the agreement and even vacated 15 days early while paying full rent for the month.

After vacating, things changed drastically. I was suddenly accused of “structural damage” for installing TVs, a water purifier, and hanging photo frames - basic, reversible fixtures in any rental. Mr Divesh and Ms Jyoti called and shouted at me repeatedly and mentally harassed me for days over calls and WhatsApp texts. No repair bills or proof were ever shared, yet INR 51,000 was deducted from my deposit without any documentation. Follow-up communication was blocked, and no email address was provided despite requests.

There were also last-minute changes regarding my indoor cats. Initially, I was told pets were allowed, but later I was asked to pay an additional amount of INR 4,000 per month for them, after I had already committed to the flat.

This review reflects my personal experience, backed by messages and agreements. The apartment had persistent pest issues, unannounced visits, unexpected demands, and a very stressful exit process. I have screenshots of all the conversations. photographs of the infested apartment and even the holes they are referring to as 'structural damage'. I’m sharing this so future tenants are aware of what they may be stepping into.

Horrifying experience.

featured_reviews.name: Zahoor Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m really disappointed with my experience living in Manopus Society. They claim to provide 24-hour water supply, but at least two days a week there’s no water at all. The management is extremely unprofessional and seems more focused on making extra money than maintaining the society.

Recently, they introduced an unfair rule that tenants are not allowed to park their vehicles inside the society, clearly so they can sell parking spaces to others. The managers are rude, often ask for bribes for even basic things, and do not treat tenants respectfully.

The amenities are in terrible condition — the so-called “gym” has broken machines and almost nothing works. On top of that, tenants are charged extra to use these already non-functional facilities.

There is zero maintenance, and living here has been very frustrating. I would not recommend this society to anyone looking for a comfortable or honest place to stay.
